title: Asking for Advice From Others Who Don’t Expect It
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Admired Leadership argues that asking people for their advice, especially when they do not expect it, is an underused way to build relationships. The post says the request signals respect and makes people feel they matter, with greater effect when the asker is talented or influential. It explains why leaders skip it: some fear it looks like needing help, others are comfortable with their own views. The move is to turn that reluctance into an advantage, since unexpected requests create an instant connection. It closes by prescribing a daily habit of asking someone for their view.
points: Asking for opinions signals respect and tells people they matter.
The effect grows with the asker's expertise or influence, yet most leaders underestimate it.
Because few leaders ask, an unexpected request stands out and quickly deepens a relationship.
The practice works upward, sideways and downward, and with clients, service providers and friends.
The prescription is concrete: ask someone for advice every day and keep a tally.
quotes: People want to know their views and opinions are valued. They are highly appreciative when leaders take the time and go out of their way to seek what they think on any issue.
Some leaders believe asking others for their views and advice is akin to declaring they need help. Others rarely ask because they are perfectly comfortable with their own views.
They fail to recognize that asking for advice, counsel, or opinions is a bonding agent stronger than glue. Upwards, sideways, and down, forging relationships is assisted with this simple act.
In a strange way, the reluctance of leaders to ask others for advice and input can actually be an advantage. Most people don’t expect it.
By asking the opinions of others who aren’t expecting it, the relationship grows closer and an instant connection is created.
Make it a habit to ask someone else for their view or advice every day. Your relationships will be closer as a result.
